import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_palette("viridis")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots using GridSpec for a more flexible layout
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(2, 2, figure=fig, hspace=0.4, wspace=0.3)

ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :]) # This subplot will span the entire bottom row

# --- Plot 1: Fraud Rate by Transaction Type ---
# Calculate the percentage of fraudulent transactions for each type
fraud_rate = df.groupby('transaction_type')['is_fraud'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False) * 100

sns.barplot(x=fraud_rate.index, y=fraud_rate.values, ax=ax1, palette="viridis")
ax1.set_title('Higher Fraud Rate in Transfers', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax1.set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Fraud Rate (%)', fontsize=12)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15)

# Add percentage labels on top of bars
for p in ax1.patches:
    ax1.annotate(f'{p.get_height():.1f}%',
                 (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                 ha='center', va='center', fontsize=10, color='black',
                 xytext=(0, 5), textcoords='offset points')

# --- Plot 2: Transaction Amount Distribution by Fraud Status ---
# Use a log scale for better visibility of amount distributions
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='is_fraud', y='amount', ax=ax2, palette="viridis", inner="quartile", cut=0)
ax2.set_yscale('log')
ax2.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'${x:,.0f}'))
ax2.set_title('Fraudulent Transactions Tend to be Larger', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax2.set_xlabel('Transaction Status', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_ylabel('Transaction Amount (Log Scale)', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_xticklabels(['Legitimate', 'Fraudulent'])

# --- Plot 3: Transaction Volume by Hour of Day ---
# Group data by hour and fraud status to see temporal patterns
hourly_transactions = df.groupby(['hour_of_day', 'is_fraud']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
hourly_transactions.columns = ['Legitimate', 'Fraudulent']

# Plotting both legitimate and fraudulent transactions over time
sns.lineplot(data=hourly_transactions, ax=ax3, markers=True, dashes=False, palette=["#440154", "#fde725"])
ax3.set_title('Fraud Peaks During Off-Hours (Early Morning & Late Night)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', loc='left')
ax3.set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2))
ax3.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.legend(title='Transaction Status')
ax3.set_xlim(0, 23)

# --- Final Touches ---
fig.suptitle('Analysis of Credit Card Fraud Patterns', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold')
# Adjust layout to prevent titles from overlapping and make room for suptitle
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
